evidenceAudit.scope: Adults in India with hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection: who to test, confirmation with HCV RNA, staging fibrosis, pan-genotypic direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Program (NVHCP), monitoring to sustained virological response at 12 weeks (SVR12), and referral of complex cases. Built on the NVHCP National Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Viral Hepatitis (2018).
findings: Anti-HCV screening, confirmation by HCV RNA, priority groups for testing and pre-treatment assessment checked against NVHCP 2018, pp. 34–35.

Treat everyone with viraemia; sofosbuvir with daclatasvir for 12 weeks without cirrhosis, sofosbuvir with velpatasvir for 12 weeks in compensated cirrhosis, and with ribavirin (or 24 weeks without ribavirin) in decompensated cirrhosis checked against pp. 36–37 (Fig. 7, Tables 8 and 9).
Monitoring schedule (Table 7), referral criteria, ribavirin dose adjustment and contraindications, amiodarone and enzyme-inducer interactions checked against pp. 36–39.
Treatment-experienced regimens (Table 12) and HIV co-infection checked against pp. 40–41.
unverifiedSections: Paediatric DAA doses are not given; NVHCP refers children to a specialised centre.
Sofosbuvir in eGFR under 30 mL/min/1.73 m² is to be used with caution at a Model Treatment Centre; exact regimen not specified.
HCV in pregnancy: DAAs are not recommended in pregnancy in the sources used; defer treatment until after delivery and seek specialist advice.
Hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance after cure in cirrhosis is not specified in the NVHCP sections used.
Drug cautions and contraindications without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.
US labels (DailyMed) were used where Indian sources give no dose; confirm against the Indian product label (CDSCO) and hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Hepatitis C is a blood-borne RNA virus. Most people infected develop chronic infection without symptoms, and over years some progress to cirrhosis, liver failure and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), at 2–4% per year once cirrhotic (NVHCP p. 34). Oral direct-acting antivirals achieve sustained virological response in over 95% (NVHCP p. 41), and every person with detectable HCV RNA should be treated (NVHCP p. 36).
keyMechanisms: HCV replicates in hepatocytes; chronic immune-mediated injury causes inflammation and fibrosis.
Fibrosis progresses faster with alcohol, male sex, HIV or HBV co-infection and immunosuppression (NVHCP p. 35).
Extrahepatic effects include cryoglobulinaemia, glomerulonephritis, insulin resistance and lichen planus (NVHCP p. 35).
DAAs block viral NS5A and NS5B proteins; SVR12 equals cure.

symptoms: Usually none; found on screening (NVHCP p. 34)
Jaundice, abdominal swelling, confusion or bleeding in decompensated cirrhosis
physicalSigns: Purpura or rash from cryoglobulinaemia (NVHCP p. 35)
redFlags: Ascites, jaundice, encephalopathy or variceal bleeding (Child-Pugh B or C): refer to a Model Treatment Centre (NVHCP p. 39)
Taking amiodarone: sofosbuvir is contraindicated (bradycardia) (NVHCP p. 38)
HBV co-infection: risk of HBV reactivation during HCV treatment
Liver mass on ultrasound: suspected HCC
precipitants: Injecting drug use with shared equipment (NVHCP p. 34)
Blood transfusion before routine screening; frequent transfusion (thalassaemia, dialysis) (NVHCP p. 34)
HIV infection; men who have sex with men; sex work (NVHCP p. 34)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Anti-HCV positive but HCV RNA not detected; no treatment needed (NVHCP p. 34).
HCV RNA negative; metabolic or alcohol history.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Reactive anti-HCV confirmed by detectable HCV RNA.
Ascites, jaundice, history of hepatic encephalopathy or variceal bleed, or Child-Pugh score 7 or more (class B and C).
HCV RNA not detected 12 weeks after the end of treatment (SVR12).

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm and stage
actions: Confirm with HCV RNA; test HBsAg and HIV (NVHCP p. 34).
APRI, FIB-4, elastography if available; ultrasound (NVHCP p. 36).
Alcohol history with brief intervention; review all medicines for interactions (NVHCP pp. 35, 39).

clinicalManagement.title: Refer complex cases
actions: Decompensated cirrhosis, treatment-experienced, chemotherapy with deranged liver tests, kidney impairment, HCC, children, thalassaemia: refer to a Model Treatment Centre (NVHCP p. 38).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat
actions: No cirrhosis: sofosbuvir + daclatasvir for 12 weeks (NVHCP Table 8).
Compensated cirrhosis: sofosbuvir + velpatasvir for 12 weeks (NVHCP Table 8).
Adherence counselling with pill counts at monthly visits (NVHCP p. 38).

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm cure
actions: HCV RNA at SVR12; detected: refer to a higher centre (NVHCP Fig. 7).
People who inject drugs: retest HCV RNA at least yearly for reinfection (NVHCP p. 40).

adjustments: Paediatric: Children: refer to a specialised centre (NVHCP p. 38).

CKD: eGFR under 30: caution, treat at Model Treatment Centre (NVHCP p. 39); dose adjustment noted for renal insufficiency (Table 8).

regimens.dose: Sofosbuvir 400 mg + velpatasvir 100 mg once daily; ribavirin 1,000 mg/day (under 75 kg) or 1,200 mg/day (75 kg or more), starting at 600 mg/day and increasing as tolerated
regimens.route: Oral (ribavirin with food in 2 divided doses)
adjustments: Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: Ribavirin: avoid if eGFR under 50; on haemodialysis 200 mg/day (NVHCP p. 38).
CLD: Model Treatment Centre only (NVHCP Table 11).
monitoring: Haemoglobin weeks 1, 2, 4, 8, 12; reduce ribavirin to 600 mg/day if haemoglobin under 10 g/dL, stop if under 8.5 g/dL (NVHCP p. 38)
contraindications: Pregnancy or no contraception; breastfeeding; haemoglobinopathy (ribavirin) (Table 10)

medicationPlan.note: All regimens and doses from NVHCP 2018: sofosbuvir 400 mg with daclatasvir 60 mg (no cirrhosis) or velpatasvir 100 mg (cirrhosis), 12 weeks; decompensated cirrhosis adds weight-based ribavirin or extends to 24 weeks. Treatment-experienced patients go to a Model Treatment Centre (Table 12). Check interactions at hep-druginteractions.org (NVHCP p. 39). Not clinically reviewed.

teaching.scope: Chronic hepatitis C in primary and specialist care.
learningObjectives: Confirm infection with HCV RNA after a reactive antibody test.
Choose the NVHCP regimen by cirrhosis status.
Know when to refer to a Model Treatment Centre.
keyPoints: Anti-HCV positive is not a diagnosis; check HCV RNA.
12 weeks of sofosbuvir-based therapy cures most patients.
Confirm cure with HCV RNA 12 weeks after treatment.
pitfalls: Treating decompensated cirrhosis outside a specialist centre.

patientEducation: Hepatitis C is curable with 12 weeks of tablets; take every dose.
A negative antibody test does not protect against future infection (NVHCP p. 37).
Cure does not prevent reinfection; avoid sharing needles.
lifestyleAndDiet: Vaccinate against hepatitis A and B if not immune (NVHCP p. 37).
mdtReferrals: Model Treatment Centre for complex cases (NVHCP p. 38)
Opioid substitution and harm reduction services for people who inject drugs (NVHCP p. 41)
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Monitoring per NVHCP Table 7; HCV RNA 12 weeks after treatment; yearly HCV RNA for ongoing risk (NVHCP pp. 36, 40).
